notes:
The header's giver is 'Nashmeira, Imperial Ward', and neither half of it survives contact with the walkthrough: bullet 1 says outright that the cutscene which BEGINS the quest is Naja Salaheem's in Aht Urhgan Whitegate (I-10), Nashmeira never appears again anywhere on the page, and 'Imperial Ward' does not resolve as a zone at all -- it is a sub-area of Aht Urhgan Whitegate, not a zone of its own. So start is moved to Naja Salaheem with the header string kept in start.raw. That is a marker MOVE, not a removal.

Demoted to medium for the gate, not the ladder: 'Quest Reqs: defeat Odin a total of 12 previous times ... choosing "Release thy knight" every time' is a running count of past battle outcomes, and no packet reports it. gates.prev holds Unwavering Resolve, which is all the schema can carry.

Step 4's Timeworn Talisman is deliberately NOT evidence even though it is obtained at that step. The page says in so many words that talismans obtained before starting the quest can be used -- so a player who happens to hold one would have the mark jump straight to step 5 and skip Naja Salaheem, the Imperial Whitegate and Yoyoroon, all three of which are still required. The two key items at step 7 and the Talisman of the rebel gods at step 6 are quest-only and anchor the back half safely.

Step 4 spans two zones (Arrapago Reef or Caedarva Mire), so it carries no zone -- a nil-zone row matches wherever you are, which is exactly the OR the page describes. Step 5's requirement is talisman AND (Sutlac OR Irmik Helvasi), which an AND-list cannot say; the Sutlac form is recorded and items_partial marks the Irmik Helvasi route as the one that could not be expressed.

Bullets 8 and 9 are two examinations of the same Entry Gate and become one step. Bullet 10 is the reward-choice cutscene that follows the win, not a step of its own. Odin's three Images are described in the note rather than recorded as mobs, because the page says 'up to 3' and never says you must kill them.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 4: two zones, so this row carries none and matches in either.
  step 5: the Irmik Helvasi route is the alternative the AND-list cannot express, hence items_partial.

notes:
Cyranuce, the header's giver, does not appear in the walkthrough even once. What the walkthrough does say is that the first thing you do is talk to Rholont in Southern San d'Oria (S) (E-7), and that the quest only flags in your log two bullets later, at the Shimmering Pondweed in Pashhow Marshlands (S) -- which is the header's ZONE but not its NPC. Cyranuce is almost certainly the cutscene at the pondweed rather than a standing entity, so start is moved to Rholont, who is a real NPC you can walk up to before the quest exists, and the header string is kept in start.raw.

Bullet 2's 'head back ... again' is the tell that this quest is continuous with The Price of Valor: you examined that pondweed already. Nothing else on the page depends on it, so it is recorded as an ordinary examine with the continuity in the note.

Hatchets are the Item Reqs and they are used at exactly one step -- logging in Jugner Forest (S) -- so the buy-them-from-Geltpix advice sits on step 1's note, where the page put it, rather than becoming a step. The four logging point grids are a note and the step carries no grid, because any of them will do.

Bullets 6 and 7 are two checks of the same Mossy Stump and become one step, with the battlefield as its own fight step. The sub-bullet under bullet 8 -- zone into Southern San d'Oria (S) from East Ronfaure (S) after a game day -- is an epilogue cutscene the page itself calls unnecessary, and the trailing Fate in Haze note is mission bookkeeping; neither is a step of this quest.

steps.note: may take more than one conversation to trigger. Buy Hatchets from Geltpix at (M-6) while you are here -- step 4 needs them and there is nowhere closer.

'again' -- you examined this during The Price of Valor. The quest flags in your log HERE, not at Rholont. Campaign teleport, or the Rolanberry Fields (S) Survival Guide which drops you on the zone line.
on the pathway. Have at least one inventory slot free or the whole cutscene has to be watched again. Recall-Jugner or the Survival Guide are the quick ways in.

logging points at (F-7), (F-10), (J-6) and (J/K-10/11) -- any of them, so no grid is recorded. The ivy is likely but not certain per attempt, so bring several hatchets; filling your inventory completely forces the key item.
the same mushrooms as step 3, back again with the ivy
lower right corner of (F-7). Check once for the cutscene, then inspect it again to enter the battlefield.

notes:
Bullet 1 is not an NPC at all -- the quest opens when you ZONE into Windurst Waters (S). The header's Robel-Akbel is kept as the start NPC because he is a real standing Windurst Waters (S) NPC and a marker on him puts you in the right zone, which is all the zone-entry trigger actually needs; the note on step 1 says what really fires it.

Bullet 4 is a genuine three-way OR: your answers to Hauberliond decide whether the New-turned Earth appears in East Ronfaure (S) (J-11), La Vaule (S) (K-9) or Jugner Forest (S) (J-5), and nothing observable tells the addon which. It is recorded as ONE step with no zone, because a zone-less row matches wherever you are -- which is exactly right for a branch where only one of the three exists for you. Making it three grouped steps would be wrong: a group means do all of them.

The key item is written 'Darkfire cinders' in bullet 2 and 'Darkfire Cinder' in bullet 5. Only the second resolves, so that is what is recorded. 'Floelight stones' resolves to nothing either, but the page says you never obtain it, so it is not used.

Bullet 7 ('grab some pickaxes') is preparation for bullet 8's mining, so the two merge and the pickaxe becomes a step requirement rather than a rung -- a pickaxe is a common item and using one as evidence would drag the mark forward for anyone who happens to carry one. Bullets 9 and 10 are both Striking Snake and stay two steps because the page really does put a Vana'diel day and a zone change between them; consecutive steps on one NPC draw one marker anyway. Striking Snake is in the PRESENT-day Metalworks, not Metalworks [S]. Bullet 12's five monsters are recorded on the fight rather than on the door, since the door is markable on its own.

notes:
Four bullets and a hole in the middle of them. Bullet 2 walks you all the way to 'the entrance to the Cloister of Flames' and bullet 3 then says 'Defeat Ifrit Prime' -- the walkthrough never says how you get into the battlefield. The header's own Description does: 'Ring the tuning fork of fire upon the protocrystal in Ifrit's Cauldron', and Notes [2] says every party member needs their own fork, which is only meaningful if the fork is spent entering. So step 3 is recorded from the Description rather than the walkthrough, at medium confidence, and the whole quest is medium for it. The target is written 'Protocrystal' because that is the only name the page ever gives it -- 'Fire Protocrystal' would be an invention.

Everything in bullet 2 after the zone line is route: the Flame Spout at (H-6) that an Ice Cluster makes recede (or you wait it out), the drop at (I-8) on map B, the drop at (H-7) on map C. That is how to get there, not what to do, so it stays in step 2's note the way the page's own sub-bullets treat the home point and Unity warp advice.

The '## After the walkthrough: Notes' section contributes NO steps -- it is party size, a 30 minute limit, one reward at a time, an Earth-day repeat timer, the Mini Fork of Fire shortcut from Trial-Size Trial by Fire, and the option of keeping the whisper for The Moonlit Path instead of turning it in. The one that matters to the ladder is the last: step 4 is a real turn-in, but a player deliberately hoarding the whisper will sit on it. The Warning line above the bullets ('Trust Magic CANNOT be used in this BCNM') and the empty [TABLE] block are not steps either. Fame 'k' is the Kazham region, level 6.

steps.note: if you are sure your Kazham fame is high enough but he will not offer it, keep talking until his text changes. The tuning fork, not the log entry, is what proves the quest is really open -- and every party member needs their own.

in from Yhoator Jungle (I-6). Map 1: the Flame Spout at (H-6) blocks the way -- trade it an Ice Cluster to make it recede or wait it out -- then on to (F-6). Map B: drop down at (I-8). Map C: the drop at (H-7), then (G-6) for the Cloister of Flames. Home point Ifrit's Cauldron #1 if you have it; the Unity 125 warp lands a short run away.

NOT in the walkthrough, which jumps straight from the Cloister entrance to the fight. Taken from the header Description -- 'Ring the tuning fork of fire upon the protocrystal' -- and from Notes [2], which only makes sense if the fork is spent entering. The page names it 'protocrystal' and nothing more, so that is the name recorded.
up to six in the arena, 30 minute limit, and Trust magic cannot be used

one reward at a time, the pact with Ifrit among them. You may instead keep the whisper for The Moonlit Path, in which case this step is never taken. Repeatable once per Earth day, which nothing in the packets reports.

notes:
The Dragoon unlock, and the page reads cleanly end to end. 'Level: 30+' with no job named is the level gate on its own -- any job -- so level is 30 and jobs stays empty; getting that backwards would lock the job quest to a job.

Bullet 1 names two NPCs in one sentence with no order given and both standing in Cargo Room A at the same grid ref, so they share a group and draw together rather than being guessed into a sequence. The header's giver, Ceraulian, is one of them, so start needs no correction.

Bullet 4 is conditional ('if you don't already happen to have some'), so buying the pickaxe is an optional step rather than a rung, and the pickaxe itself is a requirement on the excavation step rather than evidence -- holding a pickaxe proves nothing, half the players in Vana'diel carry one, and as evidence it would drag the mark forward for them. The Wyvern Egg is the honest anchor: it is obtained at step 6 and then merely carried at steps 7 and 8, which is items and not evidence, so nothing duplicates.

Bullet 10 is the reward and folds into the fight. Bullet 11 (paying to rename your wyvern) is not part of the quest, and the '## After the walkthrough: Plot Details' section is 2003 trivia about an NPC who no longer exists -- no steps come from it. The BC enemy is named on the page only as 'Wyvern', which is generic enough to be worth flagging, but it is the name the page gives and inventing a better one is not on offer.
